text:
lee (sales): NovusHealth needs a short, copy-paste capacity paragraph for procurement + a recommended reserve/autoscale plan. Their profile: steady 200 rps, short peaks to 600 rps (2-4m), avg gen ~120 tokens, user-facing p99 <= 200ms. Also call out AZ spread, prewarm, and a fallback model strategy. Can eng/infra drop numbers and a tiny load-test snippet?
sam (solutions): Quick clarifier: is 200/600 rps end-to-end app calls (one model call per request)? And which model family are they leaning to?
lee (sales): Yes one model call per request. They prefer a 70B-class model for quality but are open to 13B/6B for degraded fallback.
priya (eng): Back-of-envelope capacity notes (quantized 70B on H100/A100-class nodes, continuous batching enabled):
- Measured sustained throughput ~18-24 rps/GPU at 120 tokens with good batching and <=200ms p99 in our staging perf runs.
- Steady 200 rps -> ~9-12 GPUs technically; peak 600 rps -> ~25-34 GPUs.
Recommendation (production, conservative):
- Reserved baseline: 16 GPUs (distributed across AZs) to cover steady + operational headroom and maintenance.
- Autoscale target: max capacity 32 GPUs (allow on-demand to add ~16 GPUs for spikes).
- Prewarm pool: keep 8 GPUs prewarmed to shave cold-start for 2-4m bursts (same AZs as traffic).
- Scale rules: scale up when avg queue latency > 45ms for 45s OR GPU util > 70%; add in +4 GPU steps; cool down 3m. Scale down when util < 40% for 5m, remove -2 GPUs per step.
- Fallback policy: during sustained >3m overload route up to 40% traffic to a 13B-quantized variant; for longer degradations degrade further to a 6B-preserve-latency path. Start fallback with 5-10% sampling canary.
priya (eng): Expected tail (sized config): median ~40-120ms, p95 ~120-170ms, p99 <= 200ms. These are lab-derived estimates; we always recommend a 1-week canary under customer's real traffic.
nora (infra): Ops notes:
- Distribute reserved 16 GPUs across 3 AZs (6/5/5) for AZ-failure tolerance and procurement audit.
- Prewarm 8 GPUs as 3/3/2 across AZs.
- Canary: 1-hour progressive canary before any fallback or model switch; log sampling and perf traces for 30m.
- If they require per-route SLA in contract we must pin model version + quantization profile; otherwise we can't guarantee p99 numbers after changes.
sam (solutions): Short pasteable paragraph for procurement / questionnaire (one para + bullets):
"Redwood will provision a production footprint aligned to NovusHealth's traffic profile: steady 200 requests/sec with short bursts to 600 requests/sec (2-4 minute windows), average generation ~120 tokens/request. Baseline reserved capacity: 16 GPUs (distributed across 3 AZs) with autoscaling enabled up to 32 GPUs. An 8-GPU prewarmed burst pool reduces cold-starts for short spikes. Fallback policy: traffic can be routed to a quantized 13B model (and further to a 6B variant) under sustained overload; canary testing is used prior to rollout. Expected performance for the sized configuration: median ~40-120ms, p95 ~120-170ms, p99 <= 200ms. Logging, retention, and audit controls are configurable under the enterprise package."
sam (solutions): Cost ballpark for procurement (illustrative ranges):
- 16 reserved GPUs @ ~$5.5k/GPU/mo -> ~ $88k/mo reserved.
- Full 32 reserved -> ~ $176k/mo.
- Hybrid: 8 reserved (~$44k/mo) + autoscale on-demand to peaks -> baseline + variable burst spend (~$40k-$110k/mo) => ~ $85k-$155k/mo depending on spike frequency.
- Note: using quantized 13B fallback reduces token/throughput cost and can lower burst spend by ~30-50% depending on traffic mix.
infra-bot (bot): Created ticket INF-4400: novushealth-capacity-plan (owner: priya). Linked to sales-op:NOVUS-2024.
lee (sales): Thanks. Two final asks: 1) a tiny load-test command we can share with their infra team to reproduce the ramp/spike, 2) who will sign the procurement snippet?
priya (eng): Load test (vegeta example ramp script):
```
# phase 1: warm 0-200 rps for 3m
echo 'POST https://staging.redwood.example/v1/generate' > targets.txt
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=200 -duration=3m | vegeta report
# phase 2: ramp to 600 rps for 3m
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=600 -duration=3m | vegeta report
```
Recommendation: run 50->200->600 phases (3m each) and capture latency/p99.
priya (eng): I'll own and sign the procurement snippet after we run a 2-hour canary against their POC traffic. I'll update INF-4400 with final perf numbers.
lee (sales): Great 44d I'll paste this into their questionnaire and point to INF-4400 for engineering sign-off. Meeting with NovusHealth scheduled Tue 10am PT.
